verdict.rationale: There is concrete real-world evidence of one incident: a BLE pairing vulnerability was disclosed, Google emailed affected users ('Update on your Titan Security Key') and ran a replacement program rather than a firmware patch, showing some vulnerability-response process exists but it worked through physical device replacement, not an in-field firmware update, and users found the replacement process cumbersome. There is no published advisory list/CVE tracker or affected-model lookup tool in the evidence — docs only vaguely mention Google-engineered firmware for tamper verification. Missing for 10: a public security-advisory/CVE page, a documented affected-model/serial lookup tool, and an actual firmware-update delivery mechanism (evidence shows fixes require full device replacement, not a firmware push).
